ECONOMIC GROWTH ANALYSIS

# U.S. GDP Growth, Industry Change, Trade, and Tennessee The principal comparison is **2010–2024**. GDP values are nominal dollars, and GDP per capita divides each state-industry value by that state's estimated population. ::: {.hero-meta} MATTHEW BUTERA PYTHON / TABLEAU ::: :::
:::: ## 1. State growth The first comparison identifies the states with the strongest economic growth from 2010 to 2024. **Nominal GDP growth** measures growth in total economic output, while **GDP per capita** accounts for differences in population size. ::: {#state-growth-query .cell fig-height='6' fig-width='14' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} gdp_2010 = gdp_df.loc[gdp_df['YEAR'] == 2010].drop(columns=['YEAR','EST_POP','OVERALL_GDP','BEA_REGION']).rename(columns={'GDP': 'GDP_2010', 'GDP_CAPITA':'GDP_CAPITA_2010'}) gdp_2024 = gdp_df.loc[gdp_df['YEAR'] == 2024].drop(columns=['YEAR','EST_POP','OVERALL_GDP','BEA_REGION']).rename(columns={'GDP': 'GDP_2024', 'GDP_CAPITA':'GDP_CAPITA_2024'}) gdp_change = gdp_2010.merge(gdp_2024, on=[ 'REGION_NAME', 'STATE/REGION', 'NAICS', 'NAICS_LDESC', 'LEVEL']) gdp_change['GDP_GROWTH'] = (gdp_change['GDP_2024'] - gdp_change['GDP_2010']) / gdp_change['GDP_2010'] * 100 gdp_change['CAPITA_GROWTH'] = (gdp_change['GDP_CAPITA_2024'] - gdp_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010']) / gdp_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010'] * 100 gdp_change = gdp_change.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan) top_state_gdp = (gdp_change .loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0'] .sort_values(by='GDP_GROWTH', ascending=False) .head(10)[['REGION_NAME','GDP_GROWTH']]) top_state_capita = (gdp_change .loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0'] .sort_values(by='CAPITA_GROWTH', ascending=False) .head(10)[['REGION_NAME','CAPITA_GROWTH']]) ``` ::: ::: {#cell-fig-state-growth-chart .cell fig-height='6' fig-width='14' execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-state-growth-chart-output-1.png){#fig-state-growth-chart width=1662 height=672 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: Utah led both rankings, with nominal GDP growth of 153.2% and GDP-per-capita growth of 100.6%. Washington was a close second in per-capita growth, at 100.3%. ## 2. Industry growth To understand what's behind this, the following charts move from broad sector groups to sectors and subsectors, then show where the fastest-growing sectors expanded most. ::: {#industry-growth-query .cell fig-height='6' fig-width='11' execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} naics_change = (gdp_change .groupby('NAICS_LDESC')[['GDP_2010','GDP_CAPITA_2010','GDP_2024','GDP_CAPITA_2024']].sum() .reset_index()) naics_change_reg = (gdp_change .groupby(['REGION_NAME','STATE/REGION','NAICS_LDESC'])[['GDP_2010','GDP_CAPITA_2010','GDP_2024','GDP_CAPITA_2024']].sum() .reset_index()) naics_change['GDP_GROWTH'] = (naics_change['GDP_2024'] - naics_change['GDP_2010']) / naics_change['GDP_2010'] * 100 naics_change['CAPITA_GROWTH'] = (naics_change['GDP_CAPITA_2024'] - naics_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010']) / naics_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010'] * 100 naics_change_reg['GDP_GROWTH'] = (naics_change_reg['GDP_2024'] - naics_change_reg['GDP_2010']) / naics_change_reg['GDP_2010'] * 100 naics_change_reg['CAPITA_GROWTH'] = (naics_change_reg['GDP_CAPITA_2024'] - naics_change_reg['GDP_CAPITA_2010']) / naics_change_reg['GDP_CAPITA_2010'] * 100 naics_change['LEVEL'] = naics_change['NAICS_LDESC'].map(level_map) naics_change_reg['LEVEL'] = naics_change_reg['NAICS_LDESC'].map(level_map) naics_change_reg['BEA_REGION'] = naics_change_reg['STATE/REGION'].map(bea_regions) ``` ::: ### Broad sector-group growth The broadest industry view shows which combined sector groups produced the strongest nominal GDP growth. *For reference: Trade combines wholesale and retail trade; Manufacturing and information includes manufacturing plus digital knowledge and communication industries.* ::: {#cell-fig-sector-group-chart .cell fig-height='6' fig-width='11' execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-sector-group-chart-output-1.png){#fig-sector-group-chart width=1191 height=642 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: Arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services recorded the strongest nominal GDP growth, increasing 131.4%. Professional and business services ranked second, at 115.5%. ### Sector and subsector growth per capita The next figure ranks the five fastest-growing sectors and ten fastest-growing subsectors nationwide by GDP-per-capita growth. ::: {#cell-fig-sector-subsector-chart .cell fig-height='13' fig-width='13' execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-sector-subsector-chart-output-1.png){#fig-sector-subsector-chart width=1442 height=1442 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: The top subsectors revealed the most interesting results. Given the recent growth of AI companies in the last five years (as of 2026), the highest growth was still in AI related subsectors as of the last year in this data (2024). ### State leaders within the five fastest-growing sectors Using the five leading sectors from the previous figure, each panel ranks the ten states with the strongest per-capita growth in that sector. ::: {#cell-fig-selected-sectors-chart .cell fig-height='19' fig-width='16' execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-selected-sectors-chart-output-1.png){#fig-selected-sectors-chart width=1772 height=2102 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## 3. Growth contribution To estimate how industries contributed to overall growth, each sector's prior-year share of state GDP is multiplied by its year-over-year growth rate. The resulting measure approximates the percentage points each sector contributed to state GDP growth. $$ \text{Growth contribution}_{i,t} = \text{GDP share}_{i,t-1} \times \text{Industry growth rate}_{i,t} $$ *Because 2010 has no prior-year observation, the contribution analysis covers 2011–2024.* ::: {#contribution-query .cell fig-height='7' fig-width='11' execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} gdp_df = gdp_df.sort_values(by=['STATE/REGION','NAICS','YEAR']).reset_index(drop=True) gdp_df['YoY CHANGE'] = gdp_df.groupby(['STATE/REGION','NAICS'])['GDP'].pct_change(fill_method=None) * 100 gdp_df['GDP_SHARE'] = gdp_df['GDP'] / gdp_df['OVERALL_GDP'] gdp_df['GDP_SHARE_PY'] = gdp_df.groupby(['STATE/REGION','NAICS'])['GDP_SHARE'].shift(1) gdp_df['GROWTH_CONTRIBUTION'] = gdp_df['GDP_SHARE_PY'] * gdp_df['YoY CHANGE'] sector_contribution = (gdp_df .loc[(gdp_df['LEVEL'] == 2) & gdp_df['YEAR'].between(2011, 2024)] .groupby(['NAICS_LDESC'])['GROWTH_CONTRIBUTION'] .sum() .reset_index() .sort_values(by='GROWTH_CONTRIBUTION', ascending=False)) ``` ::: ::: {#cell-fig-national-contribution-chart .cell fig-height='7' fig-width='11' execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-national-contribution-chart-output-1.png){#fig-national-contribution-chart width=1189 height=752 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: These totals aggregate contributions to state economies across multiple years; they rank sectors' relative influence but do not represent a single national GDP growth rate. ### How contribution varies by BEA region This heatmap compares the contributions of the 12 leading national sectors across the eight BEA regions. *For both heatmaps, compare sectors across each row to identify the strongest contributors within a region or state. Values sum annual percentage-point contributions from 2011–2024 and should not be interpreted as standalone growth rates or used to rank economies.* ::: {#cell-fig-regional-contribution-chart .cell fig-height='6' fig-width='16' execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-regional-contribution-chart-output-1.png){#fig-regional-contribution-chart width=1584 height=640 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ### What drove growth in the leading per-capita states? This heatmap compares the same 12 sectors across the ten states with the strongest GDP-per-capita growth. ::: {#cell-fig-state-contribution-chart .cell fig-height='7' fig-width='16' execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-state-contribution-chart-output-1.png){#fig-state-contribution-chart width=1594 height=750 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## 4. International trade To place domestic growth in an international context, this section examines state import and export data from the U.S. Census Bureau. The first comparison sums trade values by industry from 2010 through 2024. ### Overall export and import value The chart below displays cumulative exports and imports on the same scale to compare both sector size and the balance between the two forms of trade. ::: {#cell-fig-trade-value-chart .cell fig-height='7' fig-width='12' execution_count=15} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-trade-value-chart-output-1.png){#fig-trade-value-chart width=1306 height=752 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: Manufactured goods dominated both exports and imports, accounting for approximately $20.0 trillion in exports and $31.5 trillion in imports from 2010 through 2024. ### How state trade exposure changed Trade exposure measures each state's exports or imports as a percentage of its total GDP. The KPIs below show that export exposure declined in a large majority of states. Among states where import exposure increased, the average rise was about 2 percentage points—a relatively modest shift. ::: {#trade-exposure-query .cell fig-height='4' fig-width='12' execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} export_change = (exports_df .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE']) .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2010'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ).merge((exports_df .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE']) .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2024'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ), on=['STATE/REGION']) export_change = (export_change .merge(gdp_change.loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0'][['STATE/REGION','REGION_NAME','GDP_2010','GDP_2024']], on=['STATE/REGION'])) export_change['EXPORT_2010_EXP'] = export_change['EXPORTS_2010'] / export_change['GDP_2010'] * 100 export_change['EXPORT_2024_EXP'] = export_change['EXPORTS_2024'] / export_change['GDP_2024'] * 100 export_change['EXP_GROWTH_PP'] = export_change['EXPORT_2024_EXP'] - export_change['EXPORT_2010_EXP'] import_change = (imports_df .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE']) .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2010'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ).merge((imports_df .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE']) .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2024'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ), on=['STATE/REGION']) import_change = (import_change .merge(gdp_change.loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0'][['STATE/REGION','REGION_NAME','GDP_2010','GDP_2024']], on=['STATE/REGION'])) import_change['IMPORT_2010_EXP'] = import_change['IMPORTS_2010'] / import_change['GDP_2010'] * 100 import_change['IMPORT_2024_EXP'] = import_change['IMPORTS_2024'] / import_change['GDP_2024'] * 100 import_change['IMP_GROWTH_PP'] = import_change['IMPORT_2024_EXP'] - import_change['IMPORT_2010_EXP'] negative_export_share = (export_change['EXP_GROWTH_PP'] < 0).mean() * 100 positive_import_states = import_change.loc[import_change['IMP_GROWTH_PP'] > 0] average_positive_import_growth = positive_import_states['IMP_GROWTH_PP'].mean() ``` ::: ::: {#cell-fig-trade-exposure-kpis .cell fig-height='4' fig-width='12' execution_count=17} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-trade-exposure-kpis-output-1.png){#fig-trade-exposure-kpis width=1332 height=452 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ### Which trade sectors grew fastest? The final trade comparison ranks export and import sectors by their percentage growth between 2010 and 2024. The two charts use independent scales as the leading export and import growth rates differ substantially. ::: {#trade-sector-growth-query .cell fig-height='7' fig-width='16' execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} export_change_sec = (exports_df .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','EXP_LEVEL']) .groupby(['EXP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2010'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ).merge((exports_df .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','EXP_LEVEL']) .groupby(['EXP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2024'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ), on=['EXP_NAICS_DESC']) import_change_sec = (imports_df .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','IMP_LEVEL']) .groupby(['IMP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2010'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ).merge((imports_df .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))] .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','IMP_LEVEL']) .groupby(['IMP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2024'}) .drop(columns=['YEAR']) ), on=['IMP_NAICS_DESC']) export_change_sec['EXP_SECT_GROWTH'] = (export_change_sec['EXPORTS_2024'] - export_change_sec['EXPORTS_2010']) / export_change_sec['EXPORTS_2010'] * 100 import_change_sec['IMP_SECT_GROWTH'] = (import_change_sec['IMPORTS_2024'] - import_change_sec['IMPORTS_2010']) / import_change_sec['IMPORTS_2010'] * 100 top_export_growth = export_change_sec.sort_values(by='EXP_SECT_GROWTH', ascending=False).head(5) top_import_growth = import_change_sec.sort_values(by='IMP_SECT_GROWTH', ascending=False).head(5) ``` ::: ::: {#cell-fig-trade-sector-growth-chart .cell fig-height='7' fig-width='16' execution_count=19} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-trade-sector-growth-chart-output-1.png){#fig-trade-sector-growth-chart width=1772 height=782 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: Oil, gas, minerals, and ores was the fastest-growing export sector, rising 669.8%. Among imports, used or second-hand merchandise and returned or reimported goods recorded the two largest percentage increases, at 153.3% and 147.3%, respectively. These rankings reflect percentage growth rather than total trade value. ## 5. Tennessee Tennessee ranked among the top ten states in both total GDP growth and GDP-per-capita growth. This section identifies the sectors where Tennessee was a top-five state nationally and shows how broad sector groups contributed to its year-over-year GDP growth. ::: {#cell-fig-tennessee-rank-kpis .cell fig-height='8' fig-width='12' execution_count=20} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-tennessee-rank-kpis-output-1.png){#fig-tennessee-rank-kpis width=1332 height=892 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ### Tennessee's growth-contribution timeline The stacked bars show how broad sector groups combined to produce Tennessee's annual GDP growth. Positive segments added to growth; negative segments offset it. Durable and nondurable manufacturing are excluded because they overlap the combined manufacturing-and-information group. ::: {#cell-fig-tennessee-contribution-chart .cell fig-height='8' fig-width='14' execution_count=21} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-tennessee-contribution-chart-output-1.png){#fig-tennessee-contribution-chart width=1522 height=837 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: After 2020, finance, insurance, real estate, rental, and leasing was Tennessee's most consistent source of growth, contributing approximately 1.4 to 1.9 percentage points annually through 2024. Arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services also rebounded sharply from its 2020 decline. Its average contribution during 2021–2024 was roughly three times its pre-2020 average. ::: {.source-note} **Sources:** U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis state GDP data and U.S. Census Bureau state import and export data, using the prepared project files in this repository. :::
